xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3752: Conversation transcript parsing runs on the dashboard main thread — slow opens and event-loop stalls survive PAN-3743

plan.title: Move conversation transcript parsing off the dashboard main thread
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: Conversation transcript parsing (pi/codex full-parse snapshots and the Claude initial full parse) runs on the dashboard server's main thread. 15–27 MB session JSONLs block the event loop for seconds: conversation opens sit on the loading skeleton, and the stall gaps the 15 s heartbeat past the 35 s staleness watchdog for every OTHER connected tab, producing 'Reconnecting…' flashes. Post-PAN-3743 evidence (build f33a226f0a) shows the DB-job worker lanes are clean (zero [db-jobs] slow: lines) while event-loop p99 still spikes to 200–307 ms — the stall is main-thread parsing, not DB queueing. Additionally, subscribeConversationMessages bypasses the existing getConversationByName job op with a direct main-thread call (ws-rpc.ts:890).
narratives.Proposal: Move all transcript parsing into the existing dashboard DB worker system as a new parseTranscriptSnapshot op on a dedicated fourth 'parse' worker lane (D1). The stream shells keep their parse(file) callback seam — only the callback's venue changes, so PAN-1908 wire semantics, the debounce, and the per-subscription latch are untouched (D2). The Claude initial parse uses the same op with parser='claude-initial'; its ParseResult already carries byteOffset and every priorState field, all structured-clone-safe Maps/Sets (D3). Cross-subscription coalescing reuses the existing sharedJobs machinery (D4). getConversationByName routes through its existing job op. The [db-jobs] slow: line gains bytes= for the parse op. The dead streamFullParseSnapshots twin (zero callers) is deleted so no main-thread full-parse shell lingers (D6). No chunked first payload (D5).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No chunked or streamed first-payload delivery — full-snapshot wire semantics are unchanged (FR-2).
- No frontend changes — ConversationPanel, skeleton, reducers, and the snapshot-adoption path are untouched.
- No changes to Claude incremental APPEND parsing — small tail reads stay on the main thread; only the initial full parse moves.
- No parser logic changes — venue only; parser output shapes are byte-identical.
- No new worker-pool library or process model — reuse node:worker_threads via the existing dashboard-db-worker.
- No changes to PAN-3743 lane assignments for existing ops (read/long/semantic stay as they are).
- No removal of the semantic-search lane or its timeout/cancel behavior.
- No live event-loop-monitor or staleness-reconnect test harness in unit tests — AC-1/AC-2 are verified live by the test role, not in Vitest (the Vitest job door runs inline by design).

autoDecisions.summary: Venue: dedicated 'parse' lane in the existing DB worker system (not a separate parse worker, not chunked main-thread parsing)
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body offered 'existing DB worker' vs 'dedicated parse worker'. A fourth lane inside the existing worker gives the isolation of a dedicated worker (bulk sweeps and interactive reads never queue behind a seconds-long parse) without a second process model. Parsers verified worker-clean (no server-singleton imports), so the chunked-parse fallback is not expected to trigger.

autoDecisions.summary: Edit site corrected: rewire streamResolvedFullParseSnapshots' callers, not streamFullParseSnapshots
autoDecisions.rationale: The initial PRD draft named streamFullParseSnapshots (ws-rpc.ts:114) as the edit site, but grep proves it has zero callers — the live parse call is streamResolvedFullParseSnapshots at ws-rpc.ts:235. The plan targets the live shell and deletes the dead twin so no main-thread full-parse path remains callable.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the parse(file) callback seam instead of changing stream signatures to a harness discriminator
autoDecisions.rationale: The shells already call await parse(sessionFile); swapping the callback at the one wrapper call site (streamHarnessFullParseSnapshots) leaves shell bodies, the latch, the debounce, and the existing resolved-stream test untouched — strictly smaller than the draft's signature change, same result.

autoDecisions.summary: FR-5 coalescing reuses COALESCED_OPERATIONS/sharedJobs instead of a new module-level per-file latch map
autoDecisions.rationale: The job door already coalesces concurrent identical (operation, payload) jobs and that machinery is tested. Adding the op to the set plus a lane-precedence check in workerLane() satisfies FR-5 with one line of new logic instead of a parallel coalescing mechanism.

autoDecisions.summary: Op dispatch added to BOTH executeInline (dashboard-db-task.ts) and runJob (dashboard-db-worker.ts)
autoDecisions.rationale: The draft mentioned only runInline; the worker thread has its own duplicated switch and DashboardDbOperation union. Adding the op to only one switch silently breaks the other path — both are named in the work item and locked by the routing test.

autoDecisions.summary: No chunked first payload (issue-direction option not taken)
autoDecisions.rationale: Chunked streaming would change wire semantics (FR-2 forbids) for a latency win NFR-2 does not require — first payload may take the same wall-clock time as today; it only must not block the loop.
